ESV.1: “You shall make an altar on which to burn incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.
ESV.2: A cubit  shall be its length, and a cubit its breadth. It shall be square, and two cubits shall be its height. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.
ESV.3: You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top and around its sides and its horns. And you shall make a molding of gold around it.
ESV.4: And you shall make two golden rings for it. Under its molding on two opposite sides of it you shall make them, and they shall be holders for poles with which to carry it.
ESV.5: You shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
ESV.6: And you shall put it in front of the veil that is above the ark of the testimony, in front of the mercy seat that is above the testimony, where I will meet with you.
ESV.7: And Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it. Every morning when he dresses the lamps he shall burn it,
ESV.8: and when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it, a regular incense offering before the LORD throughout your generations.
ESV.9: You shall not offer unauthorized incense on it, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering, and you shall not pour a drink offering on it.
ESV.10: Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year. With the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement for it once in the year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”
ESV.12: “When you take the census of the people of Israel, then each shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when you number them, that there be no plague among them when you number them.
ESV.13: Each one who is numbered in the census shall give this: half a shekel  according to the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel is twenty gerahs),  half a shekel as an offering to the LORD.
ESV.14: Everyone who is numbered in the census, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the LORD's offering.
ESV.15: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, when you give the LORD's offering to make atonement for your lives.
ESV.16: You shall take the atonement money from the people of Israel and shall give it for the service of the tent of meeting, that it may bring the people of Israel to remembrance before the LORD, so as to make atonement for your lives.”
ESV.18: “You shall also make a basin of bronze, with its stand of bronze, for washing. You shall put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it,
ESV.19: with which Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet.
ESV.20: When they go into the tent of meeting, or when they come near the altar to minister, to burn a food offering  to the LORD, they shall wash with water, so that they may not die.
ESV.21: They shall wash their hands and their feet, so that they may not die. It shall be a statute forever to them, even to him and to his offspring throughout their generations.”
ESV.23: “Take the finest spices: of liquid myrrh 500 shekels, and of sweet-smelling cinnamon half as much, that is, 250, and 250 of aromatic cane,
ESV.24: and 500 of cassia, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, and a hin  of olive oil.
ESV.25: And you shall make of these a sacred anointing oil blended as by the perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
ESV.26: With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
ESV.27: and the table and all its utensils, and the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
ESV.28: and the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils and the basin and its stand.
ESV.29: You shall consecrate them, that they may be most holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
ESV.30: You shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them, that they may serve me as priests.
ESV.31: And you shall say to the people of Israel, ‘This shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
ESV.32: It shall not be poured on the body of an ordinary person, and you shall make no other like it in composition. It is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
ESV.33: Whoever compounds any like it or whoever puts any of it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.’”
ESV.34: The LORD said to Moses, “Take sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum, sweet spices with pure frankincense (of each shall there be an equal part),
ESV.35: and make an incense blended as by the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
ESV.36: You shall beat some of it very small, and put part of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting where I shall meet with you. It shall be most holy for you.
ESV.37: And the incense that you shall make according to its composition, you shall not make for yourselves. It shall be for you holy to the LORD.
ESV.38: Whoever makes any like it to use as perfume shall be cut off from his people.”

NKJV.1: “You shall make an altar to burn incense on; you shall make it of acacia wood.
NKJV.2: A cubit shall be its length and a cubit its width—it shall be square—and two cubits shall be its height. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.
NKJV.3: And you shall overlay its top, its sides all around, and its horns with pure gold; and you shall make for it a molding of gold all around.
NKJV.4: Two gold rings you shall make for it, under the molding on both its sides. You shall place them on its two sides, and they will be holders for the poles with which to bear it.
NKJV.5: You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
NKJV.6: And you shall put it before the veil that is before the ark of the Testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony, where I will meet with you.
NKJV.7: “Aaron shall burn on it sweet incense every morning; when he tends the lamps, he shall burn incense on it.
NKJV.8: And when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he shall burn incense on it, a perpetual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
NKJV.9: You shall not offer strange incense on it, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering; nor shall you pour a drink offering on it.
NKJV.10: And Aaron shall make atonement upon its horns once a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonement; once a year he shall make atonement upon it throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”
NKJV.11: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.12: “When you take the census of the children of Israel for their number, then every man shall give a ransom for himself to the LORD, when you number them, that there may be no plague among them when you number them.
NKJV.13: This is what everyone among those who are numbered shall give: half a shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary (a shekel is twenty gerahs). The half-shekel shall be an offering to the LORD.
NKJV.14: Everyone included among those who are numbered, from twenty years old and above, shall give an offering to the LORD.
NKJV.15: The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel, when you give an offering to the LORD, to make atonement for yourselves.
NKJV.16: And you shall take the atonement money of the children of Israel, and shall appoint it for the service of the tabernacle of meeting, that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before the LORD, to make atonement for yourselves.”
NKJV.17: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.18: “You shall also make a laver of bronze, with its base also of bronze, for washing. You shall put it between the tabernacle of meeting and the altar. And you shall put water in it,
NKJV.19: for Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet in water from it.
NKJV.20: When they go into the tabernacle of meeting, or when they come near the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire to the LORD, they shall wash with water, lest they die.
NKJV.21: So they shall wash their hands and their feet, lest they die. And it shall be a statute forever to them—to him and his descendants throughout their generations.”
NKJV.22: Moreover the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.23: “Also take for yourself quality spices—five hundred shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much sweet-smelling cinnamon (two hundred and fifty shekels), two hundred and fifty shekels of sweet-smelling cane,
NKJV.24: five hundred shekels of cassia, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, and a hin of olive oil.
NKJV.25: And you shall make from these a holy anointing oil, an ointment compounded according to the art of the perfumer. It shall be a holy anointing oil.
NKJV.26: With it you shall anoint the tabernacle of meeting and the ark of the Testimony;
NKJV.27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense;
NKJV.28: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the laver and its base.
NKJV.29: You shall consecrate them, that they may be most holy; whatever touches them must be holy.
NKJV.30: And you shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them, that they may minister to Me as priests.
NKJV.31: “And you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: ‘This shall be a holy anointing oil to Me throughout your generations.
NKJV.32: It shall not be poured on man’s flesh; nor shall you make any other like it, according to its composition. It is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
NKJV.33: Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever puts any of it on an outsider, shall be cut off from his people.’ ”
NKJV.34: And the LORD said to Moses: “Take sweet spices, stacte and onycha and galbanum, and pure frankincense with these sweet spices; there shall be equal amounts of each.
NKJV.35: You shall make of these an incense, a compound according to the art of the perfumer, salted, pure, and holy.
NKJV.36: And you shall beat some of it very fine, and put some of it before the Testimony in the tabernacle of meeting where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
NKJV.37: But as for the incense which you shall make, you shall not make any for yourselves, according to its composition. It shall be to you holy for the LORD.
NKJV.38: Whoever makes any like it, to smell it, he shall be cut off from his people.”

NASB.1: 'Moreover, you shall make an altar as a place for burning incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.
NASB.2: 'Its length [shall be] a cubit, and its width a cubit, it shall be square, and its height [shall be] two cubits; its horns [shall be] of one piece with it.
NASB.3: 'You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top and its sides all around, and its horns; and you shall make a gold molding all around for it.
NASB.4: 'You shall make two gold rings for it under its molding; you shall make [them] on its two side walls-- on opposite sides-- and they shall be holders for poles with which to carry it.
NASB.5: 'You shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
NASB.6: 'You shall put this altar in front of the veil that is near the ark of the testimony, in front of the mercy seat that is over [the ark of] the testimony, where I will meet with you.
NASB.7: 'Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it; he shall burn it every morning when he trims the lamps.
NASB.8: 'When Aaron trims the lamps at twilight, he shall burn incense. [There shall be] perpetual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
NASB.9: 'You shall not offer any strange incense on this altar, or burnt offering or meal offering; and you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.
NASB.10: 'Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year; he shall make atonement on it with the blood of the sin offering of atonement once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.'
NASB.11: The LORD also spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.12: 'When you take a census of the sons of Israel to number them, then each one of them shall give a ransom for himself to the LORD, when you number them, so that there will be no plague among them when you number them.
NASB.13: 'This is what everyone who is numbered shall give: half a shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel is twenty gerahs), half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.
NASB.14: 'Everyone who is numbered, from twenty years old and over, shall give the contribution to the LORD.
NASB.15: 'The rich shall not pay more and the poor shall not pay less than the half shekel, when you give the contribution to the LORD to make atonement for yourselves.
NASB.16: 'You shall take the atonement money from the sons of Israel and shall give it for the service of the tent of meeting, that it may be a memorial for the sons of Israel before the LORD, to make atonement for yourselves.'
NASB.17: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.18: 'You shall also make a laver of bronze, with its base of bronze, for washing; and you shall put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it.
NASB.19: 'Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it;
NASB.20: when they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water, so that they will not die; or when they approach the altar to minister, by offering up in smoke a fire [sacrifice] to the LORD.
NASB.21: 'So they shall wash their hands and their feet, so that they will not die; and it shall be a perpetual statute for them, for Aaron and his descendants throughout their generations.'
NASB.22: Moreover, the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.23: 'Take also for yourself the finest of spices: of flowing myrrh five hundred [shekels], and of fragrant cinnamon half as much, two hundred and fifty, and of fragrant cane two hundred and fifty,
NASB.24: and of cassia five hundred, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, and of olive oil a hin.
NASB.25: 'You shall make of these a holy anointing oil, a perfume mixture, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
NASB.26: 'With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
NASB.27: and the table and all its utensils, and the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
NASB.28: and the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the laver and its stand.
NASB.29: 'You shall also consecrate them, that they may be most holy; whatever touches them shall be holy.

CSB17.1: “You are to make an altar for the burning of incense; make it of acacia wood. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.2: It must be square, eighteen inches long and eighteen inches wide; <sup>[1]</sup> it must be thirty-six inches high. <sup>[2]</sup> Its horns must be of one piece with it.
CSB17.3: Overlay its top, all around its sides, and its horns with pure gold; make a gold molding all around it.
CSB17.4: Make two gold rings for it under the molding on two of its sides; put these on opposite sides of it to be holders for the poles to carry it with.
CSB17.5: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
CSB17.6: “You are to place the altar in front of the curtain by the ark of the testimony — in front of the mercy seat that is over the testimony — where I will meet with you.
CSB17.7: Aaron must burn fragrant incense on it; he must burn it every morning when he tends the lamps. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: When Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he must burn incense. There is to be an incense offering before the LORD throughout your generations.
CSB17.9: You must not offer unauthorized incense on it, <sup>ⓝ</sup> or a burnt or grain offering; you are not to pour a drink offering on it.
CSB17.10: “Once a year Aaron is to perform the atonement ceremony for the altar. Throughout your generations he is to perform the atonement ceremony for <sup>[3]</sup> it once a year, with the blood of the sin offering for atonement on the horns. <sup>ⓐ</sup> The altar is especially holy to the LORD.”
CSB17.12: “When you take a census <sup>ⓑ</sup> of the Israelites to register them, each of the men must pay a ransom <sup>ⓒ</sup> for his life to the LORD as they are registered. Then no plague <sup>ⓓ</sup> will come on them as they are registered.
CSB17.13: Everyone who is registered must pay half a shekel <sup>[4]</sup> according to the sanctuary shekel (twenty gerahs to the shekel). This half shekel is a contribution to the LORD. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.14: Each man who is registered, twenty years old or more, must give this contribution to the LORD.
CSB17.15: The wealthy may not give more and the poor may not give less <sup>ⓕ</sup> than half a shekel when giving the contribution to the LORD to atone for <sup>[5]</sup> your lives.
CSB17.16: Take the atonement price <sup>[6]</sup> from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will serve as a reminder for the Israelites before the LORD to atone for your lives.” <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.18: “Make a bronze basin <sup>ⓗ</sup> for washing and a bronze stand for it. Set it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
CSB17.19: Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet from the basin.
CSB17.20: Whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister by burning an offering to the LORD, they must wash with water so that they will not die.
CSB17.21: They must wash their hands and feet so that they will not die; this is to be a permanent statute <sup>ⓘ</sup> for them, for Aaron and his descendants throughout their generations.”
CSB17.23: “Take for yourself the finest spices: <sup>ⓙ</sup> 12½ pounds <sup>[7]</sup> of liquid myrrh, half as much (6¼ pounds <sup>[8]</sup>) of fragrant cinnamon, 6¼ pounds of fragrant cane,
CSB17.24: 12½ pounds of cassia (by the sanctuary shekel), and a gallon <sup>[9]</sup> of olive oil. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.25: Prepare from these a holy anointing oil, a scented blend, the work of a perfumer; it will be holy anointing oil. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.26: “With it you are to anoint <sup>ⓜ</sup> the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony,
CSB17.27: the table with all its utensils, the lampstand with its utensils, the altar of incense,
CSB17.28: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
CSB17.29: Consecrate them and they will be especially holy. Whatever touches them will be consecrated.
CSB17.30: Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate <sup>ⓝ</sup> them to serve me as priests.
CSB17.31: “Tell the Israelites: This will be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
CSB17.32: It must not be used for ordinary anointing on a person’s body, and you must not make anything like it using its formula. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
CSB17.33: Anyone who blends something like it or puts some of it on an unauthorized person must be cut off <sup>ⓐ</sup> from his people.”
CSB17.34: The LORD said to Moses: “Take fragrant spices: stacte, onycha, and galbanum; the spices and pure frankincense are to be in equal measures.
CSB17.35: Prepare expertly blended incense from these; it is to be seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
CSB17.36: Grind some of it into a fine powder and put some in front of the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It must be especially holy <sup>ⓑ</sup> to you.
CSB17.37: As for the incense you are making, you must not make any for yourselves using its formula. It is to be regarded by you as holy — belonging to the LORD.
CSB17.38: Anyone who makes something like it to smell its fragrance must be cut off from his people.”

NLT.1: “Then make another altar of acacia wood for burning incense.
NLT.2: Make it 18 inches square and 36 inches high, with horns at the corners carved from the same piece of wood as the altar itself.
NLT.3: Overlay the top, sides, and horns of the altar with pure gold, and run a gold molding around the entire altar.
NLT.4: Make two gold rings, and attach them on opposite sides of the altar below the gold molding to hold the carrying poles.
NLT.5: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
NLT.6: Place the incense altar just outside the inner curtain that shields the Ark of the Covenant, in front of the Ark’s cover — the place of atonement — that covers the tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant. I will meet with you there.
NLT.7: “Every morning when Aaron maintains the lamps, he must burn fragrant incense on the altar.
NLT.8: And each evening when he lights the lamps, he must again burn incense in the LORD’s presence. This must be done from generation to generation.
NLT.9: Do not offer any unholy incense on this altar, or any burnt offerings, grain offerings, or liquid offerings.
NLT.10: “Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing its horns with blood from the offering made to purify the people from their sin. This will be a regular, annual event from generation to generation, for this is the LORD’s most holy altar.”
NLT.11: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.12: “Whenever you take a census of the people of Israel, each man who is counted must pay a ransom for himself to the LORD. Then no plague will strike the people as you count them.
NLT.13: Each person who is counted must give a small piece of silver as a sacred offering to the LORD. (This payment is half a shekel, based on the sanctuary shekel, which equals twenty gerahs.)
NLT.14: All who have reached their twentieth birthday must give this sacred offering to the LORD.
NLT.15: When this offering is given to the LORD to purify your lives, making you right with him, the rich must not give more than the specified amount, and the poor must not give less.
NLT.16: Receive this ransom money from the Israelites, and use it for the care of the Tabernacle. It will bring the Israelites to the LORD’s attention, and it will purify your lives.”
NLT.17: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.18: “Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand. Place it between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it with water.
NLT.19: Aaron and his sons will wash their hands and feet there.
NLT.20: They must wash with water whenever they go into the Tabernacle to appear before the LORD and when they approach the altar to burn up their special gifts to the LORD — or they will die!
NLT.21: They must always wash their hands and feet, or they will die. This is a permanent law for Aaron and his descendants, to be observed from generation to generation.”
NLT.22: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.23: “Collect choice spices — 12 1⁄2 pounds of pure myrrh, 6 1⁄4 pounds of fragrant cinnamon, 6 1⁄4 pounds of fragrant calamus,
NLT.24: and 12 1⁄2 pounds of cassia — as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel. Also get one gallon of olive oil.
NLT.25: Like a skilled incense maker, blend these ingredients to make a holy anointing oil.
NLT.26: Use this sacred oil to anoint the Tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant,
NLT.27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its accessories, the incense altar,
NLT.28: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the washbasin with its stand.
NLT.29: Consecrate them to make them absolutely holy. After this, whatever touches them will also become holy.
NLT.30: “Anoint Aaron and his sons also, consecrating them to serve me as priests.
NLT.31: And say to the people of Israel, ‘This holy anointing oil is reserved for me from generation to generation.
NLT.32: It must never be used to anoint anyone else, and you must never make any blend like it for yourselves. It is holy, and you must treat it as holy.
NLT.33: Anyone who makes a blend like it or anoints someone other than a priest will be cut off from the community.’”
NLT.34: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Gather fragrant spices — resin droplets, mollusk shell, and galbanum — and mix these fragrant spices with pure frankincense, weighed out in equal amounts.
NLT.35: Using the usual techniques of the incense maker, blend the spices together and sprinkle them with salt to produce a pure and holy incense.
NLT.36: Grind some of the mixture into a very fine powder and put it in front of the Ark of the Covenant, where I will meet with you in the Tabernacle. You must treat this incense as most holy.
NLT.37: Never use this formula to make this incense for yourselves. It is reserved for the LORD, and you must treat it as holy.
NLT.38: Anyone who makes incense like this for personal use will be cut off from the community.”

WEB.1: “You shall make an altar to burn incense on. You shall make it of acacia wood.
WEB.2: Its length shall be a cubit,  and its width a cubit. It shall be square, and its height shall be two cubits. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.
WEB.3: You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top, its sides around it, and its horns; and you shall make a gold molding around it.
WEB.4: You shall make two golden rings for it under its molding; on its two ribs, on its two sides you shall make them; and they shall be for places for poles with which to bear it.
WEB.5: You shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
WEB.6: You shall put it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
WEB.7: Aaron shall burn incense of sweet spices on it every morning. When he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
WEB.8: When Aaron lights the lamps at evening, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before Yahweh throughout your generations.
WEB.9: You shall offer no strange incense on it, nor burnt offering, nor meal offering; and you shall pour no drink offering on it.
WEB.10: Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once in the year; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement once in the year he shall make atonement for it throughout your generations. It is most holy to Yahweh.”
WEB.12: “When you take a census of the children of Israel, according to those who are counted among them, then each man shall give a ransom for his soul to Yahweh, when you count them; that there be no plague among them when you count them.
WEB.13: They shall give this, everyone who passes over to those who are counted, half a shekel after the shekel  of the sanctuary (the shekel is twenty gerahs ); half a shekel for an offering to Yahweh.
WEB.14: Everyone who passes over to those who are counted, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering to Yahweh.
WEB.15: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel,  when they give the offering of Yahweh, to make atonement for your souls.
WEB.16: You shall take the atonement money from the children of Israel, and shall appoint it for the service of the Tent of Meeting; that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before Yahweh, to make atonement for your souls.”
WEB.18: “You shall also make a basin of brass, and its base of brass, in which to wash. You shall put it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it.
WEB.19: Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet in it.
WEB.20: When they go into the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water, that they not die; or when they come near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire to Yahweh.
WEB.21: So they shall wash their hands and their feet, that they not die: and it shall be a statute forever to them, even to him and to his descendants throughout their generations.”
WEB.22: Moreover Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
WEB.23: “Also take fine spices: of liquid myrrh, five hundred shekels;  and of fragrant cinnamon half as much, even two hundred and fifty; and of fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty;
WEB.24: and of cassia five hundred, after the shekel of the sanctuary; and a hin of olive oil.
WEB.25: You shall make it a holy anointing oil, a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer: it shall be a holy anointing oil.
WEB.26: You shall use it to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the testimony,
WEB.27: the table and all its articles, the lamp stand and its accessories, the altar of incense,
WEB.28: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its base.
WEB.29: You shall sanctify them, that they may be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.
WEB.30: You shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify them, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office.
WEB.31: You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘This shall be a holy anointing oil to me throughout your generations.
WEB.32: It shall not be poured on man’s flesh, and do not make any like it, according to its composition. It is holy. It shall be holy to you.
WEB.33: Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever puts any of it on a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people.’”
WEB.34: Yahweh said to Moses, “Take to yourself sweet spices, gum resin, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure frankincense: there shall be an equal weight of each;
WEB.35: and you shall make incense of it, a perfume after the art of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy:
WEB.36: and you shall beat some of it very small, and put some of it before the testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be to you most holy.
WEB.37: The incense which you shall make, according to its composition you shall not make for yourselves: it shall be to you holy for Yahweh.
WEB.38: Whoever shall make any like that, to smell of it, he shall be cut off from his people.”

AMP.1: "You shall make an altar upon which to burn incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.

NRSVCE.23: Take the finest spices: of liquid myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet-smelling cinnamon half as much, that is, two hundred fifty, and two hundred fifty of aromatic cane,
NRSVCE.24: and five hundred of cassia — measured by the sanctuary shekel — and a hin of olive oil;
NRSVCE.25: and you shall make of these a sacred anointing oil blended as by the perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.
NRSVCE.26: With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the covenant,
NRSVCE.27: and the table and all its utensils, and the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
NRSVCE.28: and the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
NRSVCE.29: you shall consecrate them, so that they may be most holy; whatever touches them will become holy.
NRSVCE.30: You shall anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them, in order that they may serve me as priests.
NRSVCE.31: You shall say to the Israelites, “This shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
NRSVCE.32: It shall not be used in any ordinary anointing of the body, and you shall make no other like it in composition; it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
NRSVCE.33: Whoever compounds any like it or whoever puts any of it on an unqualified person shall be cut off from the people.”
NRSVCE.34: The LORD said to Moses: Take sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum, sweet spices with pure frankincense (an equal part of each),
NRSVCE.35: and make an incense blended as by the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy;
NRSVCE.36: and you shall beat some of it into powder, and put part of it before the covenant in the tent of meeting where I shall meet with you; it shall be for you most holy.
NRSVCE.37: When you make incense according to this composition, you shall not make it for yourselves; it shall be regarded by you as holy to the LORD.
NRSVCE.38: Whoever makes any like it to use as perfume shall be cut off from the people.

NIV.1:
The Altar of Incense
“Make an altar of acacia wood for burning incense.
NIV.2: It is to be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high—its horns of one piece with it.
NIV.3: Overlay the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it.
NIV.4: Make two gold rings for the altar below the molding—two on opposite sides—to hold the poles used to carry it.
NIV.5: Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
NIV.6: Put the altar in front of the curtain that is before the ark of the Testimony—before the atonement cover that is over the Testimony—where I will meet with you.
NIV.7: “Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps.
NIV.8: He must burn incense again when he lights the lamps at twilight so incense will burn regularly before the Lord for the generations to come.
NIV.9: Do not offer on this altar any other incense or any burnt offering or grain offering, and do not pour a drink offering on it.
NIV.10: Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns. This annual atonement must be made with the blood of the atoning sin offering for the generations to come. It is most holy to the Lord.”
NIV.11:
Atonement Money
Then the Lord said to Moses,
NIV.12: “When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each one must pay the Lord a ransom for his life at the time he is counted. Then no plague will come on them when you number them.
NIV.13: Each one who crosses over to those already counted is to give a half shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the Lord.
NIV.14: All who cross over, those twenty years old or more, are to give an offering to the Lord.
NIV.15: The rich are not to give more than a half shekel and the poor are not to give less when you make the offering to the Lord to atone for your lives.
NIV.16: Receive the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, making atonement for your lives.”
NIV.17:
Basin for Washing
Then the Lord said to Moses,
NIV.18: “Make a bronze basin, with its bronze stand, for washing. Place it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
NIV.19: Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet with water from it.
NIV.20: Whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water so that they will not die. Also, when they approach the altar to minister by presenting an offering made to the Lord by fire,
NIV.21: they shall wash their hands and feet so that they will not die. This is to be a lasting ordinance for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.”
NIV.22:
Anointing Oil
Then the Lord said to Moses,
NIV.23: “Take the following fine spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much (that is, 250 shekels) of fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
NIV.24: 500 shekels of cassia—all according to the sanctuary shekel—and a hin of olive oil.
NIV.25: Make these into a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It will be the sacred anointing oil.
NIV.26: Then use it to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark of the Testimony,
NIV.27: the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its accessories, the altar of incense,
NIV.28: the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
NIV.29: You shall consecrate them so they will be most holy, and whatever touches them will be holy.
NIV.30: “Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them so they may serve me as priests.
NIV.31: Say to the Israelites, ‘This is to be my sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.
NIV.32: Do not pour it on men’s bodies and do not make any oil with the same formula. It is sacred, and you are to consider it sacred.
NIV.33: Whoever makes perfume like it and whoever puts it on anyone other than a priest must be cut off from his people.’”
NIV.34:
Incense
Then the Lord said to Moses, “Take fragrant spices—gum resin, onycha and galbanum—and pure frankincense, all in equal amounts,
NIV.35: and make a fragrant blend of incense, the work of a perfumer. It is to be salted and pure and sacred.
NIV.36: Grind some of it to powder and place it in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
NIV.37: Do not make any incense with this formula for yourselves; consider it holy to the Lord.
NIV.38: Whoever makes any like it to enjoy its fragrance must be cut off from his people.”

NET.1: “You are to make an altar for burning incense; you are to make it of acacia wood.
NET.2: Its length is to be a foot and a half and its width a foot and a half; it will be square. Its height is to be three feet, with its horns of one piece with it.
NET.3: You are to overlay it with pure gold — its top, its four walls, and its horns — and make a surrounding border of gold for it.
NET.4: You are to make two gold rings for it under its border, on its two flanks; you are to make them on its two sides. The rings will be places for poles to carry it with.
NET.5: You are to make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
NET.6: “You are to put it in front of the curtain that is before the ark of the testimony (before the atonement lid that is over the testimony), where I will meet you.
NET.7: Aaron is to burn sweet incense on it morning by morning; when he attends to the lamps he is to burn incense.
NET.8: When Aaron sets up the lamps around sundown he is to burn incense on it; it is to be a regular incense offering before the LORD throughout your generations.
NET.9: You must not offer strange incense on it, nor burnt offering, nor meal offering, and you must not pour out a drink offering on it.
NET.10: Aaron is to make atonement on its horns once in the year with some of the blood of the sin offering for atonement; once in the year he is to make atonement on it throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.”
NET.12: “When you take a census of the Israelites according to their number, then each man is to pay a ransom for his life to the LORD when you number them, so that there will be no plague among them when you number them.
NET.13: Everyone who crosses over to those who are numbered is to pay this: a half shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary (a shekel weighs twenty gerahs). The half shekel is to be an offering to the LORD.
NET.14: Everyone who crosses over to those numbered, from twenty years old and up, is to pay an offering to the LORD.
NET.15: The rich are not to increase it, and the poor are not to pay less than the half shekel when giving the offering of the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.
NET.16: You are to receive the atonement money from the Israelites and give it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives.”
NET.18: “You are also to make a large bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. You are to put it between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it,
NET.19: and Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and their feet from it.
NET.20: When they enter the tent of meeting, they must wash with water so that they do not die. Also, when they approach the altar to minister by burning incense as an offering made by fire to the LORD,
NET.21: they must wash their hands and their feet so that they do not die. And this will be a perpetual ordinance for them and for their descendants throughout their generations.”
NET.23: “Take choice spices: twelve and a half pounds of free-flowing myrrh, half that — about six and a quarter pounds — of sweet-smelling cinnamon, six and a quarter pounds of sweet-smelling cane,
NET.24: and twelve and a half pounds of cassia, all weighed according to the sanctuary shekel, and four quarts of olive oil.
NET.25: You are to make this into a sacred anointing oil, a perfumed compound, the work of a perfumer. It will be sacred anointing oil.
NET.26: “With it you are to anoint the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony,
NET.27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
NET.28: the altar for the burnt offering and all its utensils, and the laver and its base.
NET.29: So you are to sanctify them, and they will be most holy; anything that touches them will be holy.
NET.30: “You are to anoint Aaron and his sons and sanctify them, so that they may minister as my priests.
NET.31: And you are to tell the Israelites: ‘This is to be my sacred anointing oil throughout your generations.
NET.32: It must not be applied to people’s bodies, and you must not make any like it with the same recipe. It is holy, and it must be holy to you.
NET.33: Whoever makes perfume like it and whoever puts any of it on someone not a priest will be cut off from his people.’”
NET.34: The LORD said to Moses: “Take spices, gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense of equal amounts
NET.35: and make it into an incense, a perfume, the work of a perfumer. It is to be finely ground, and pure and sacred.
NET.36: You are to beat some of it very fine and put some of it before the ark of the testimony in the tent of meeting where I will meet with you; it is to be most holy to you.
NET.37: And the incense that you are to make, you must not make for yourselves using the same recipe; it is to be most holy to you, belonging to the LORD.
NET.38: Whoever makes anything like it, to use as perfume, will be cut off from his people.”
